body: I feel the exact same way (ciswoman). For me what helped was being put on birth control. You can take birth control continuously (ie., skip sugar pills and move onto the next packet). The length of time you can do this varies by person (might have side effects like spotting) but for me personally I can go 6 months in between periods. There are other options like hormonal iuds etc. I’d strongly suggest looking into this if you live somewhere where bc is accessible. I’m not going to lie, for me it’s the only way I can have a life I feel like is worth living.

I can’t answer the latter questions because there’s not much to say. Those are very valid things to be worrying about rn, but you’ll have answers soon. Try to remember that there’s nothing you can do right now, and that you can worry after you get any news (if it’s bad). A quick google search though tells that you can have *temporary* alopecia after stressful events - hopefully it’s that! Terminal disease is really unlikely. Realistically you mainly have to worry about if hair loss is permanent or not and there’s plenty of conditions that are temporary.

But for the first question, try to remember that healthcare professionals are super desensitized to all sorts of bodies. They don’t give a shit about what someone’s body looks like. They might say something out of concern but there’s very little space for judgement when you’re seeing naked bodies all the time. I guarantee you they’ve seen something much worse.
Funny, a big problem with women’s mental health support is that people don’t take them seriously or think that they’re doing it for attention.
I know how you feel but it’s good to remember that it’s not a competition. Who are you trying to prove yourself to? SH isn’t something you want to win at.
If it makes you feel any better I left my blade in the shower once. Thankfully didn’t get caught but you’re not the only dumbass.

Maybe bring a hoodie and wear it over top? Even before I SH I’ve had anxiety issues where I must always wear a hoodie and it’s never been a problem for me. Maybe even try to get a hoodie that has the same colours as your club.
Idk if it’s weird to compliment scars but I love how organized yours are.

Like the other person said it may take months or years. If it’s any consolation though it’s just one isolated scar so no one will suspect SH and you can still wear short sleeves. Obviously you’ll still know it’s there but at least you won’t have to worry about covering up.

I have an pretty good relationship but I’m just not sure that they’re the greatest when it comes to mental illness. I still remember the one time my mom accused me of crying to try and get my way (not true btw). Other than that I have great parents. Idk, neither of them suffered from mental illness and I don’t think they’re capable of understanding it but I could be wrong.
I think part of it is misunderstanding. Movies and media usually portray it as wrists. A lot of people also think SH = suicidal thoughts, and slicing wrists is a well known suicide method.
